author: National Geographic
description:
Millions of pangolins have been taken from the wild across Africa in recent decades, fueling concerns about their survival. To prepare rescued pangolins for a return to the wild, conservationists at the Tikki Hywood Foundation are learning how best to care for them. Here's more on the efforts to protect these heavily trafficked mammals: https://on.natgeo.com/0b2048

title: Presented by @ROLEX. National Geographic photographer Marcus Westberg filmed a pangolin feeding.

author: National Geographic
description:
In this full episode of Mysteries of Ancient Medicine from National Geographic, explore the startling and unexpected origins of human medical practice.

From Europeans consuming powdered human mummies to Austrians ingesting lethal arsenic for beauty and strength, history is filled with bizarre and deadly remedies. Journey to Guatemala, to an ancient Mayan sweat bath carved with a deity that exposes healing practices centered on mothers and childbirth. Learn how ancient civilizations treated illness, childbirth, and spiritual health, and discover the extreme paths humanity took in the quest for survival. 

Mysteries of Ancient Medicine | S1 E4 "Mummy Medicine, King of Poisons, Maya Sweat Baths"
